selected.look_here_first: Look for large, pale trumpet-shaped flowers with a yellow throat, thick rough-textured oval leaves and a persistent fleshy fruit; check leaf surfaces and calyx before distinguishing from other Cordia.
Look for small white five-petaled flowers above divided lower leaves, then inspect the rounded clusters of dry fruits with hooked persistent styles.
Inspect the fan-shaped pleated leaves and their smooth, unarmed petioles, then check the branching flower or fruit stalks emerging above the low crown.
Look for pinnate leaves with many oval, smooth-edged leaflets, paired stipular spines on twigs, hanging clusters of pea-shaped white flowers and flat pods.
Inspect the stiff prickly leaf margins and rounded, clasping leaf bases, yellow dandelion-like flower heads, and milky sap; compare with less-prickly Sonchus oleraceus.
